name: llmc_attention_forward
goal: Port attention_forward_harness.cu (llm.c dev/cuda/attention_forward.cu, fp32 build) to idiomatic SYCL 2020 with zero dpct helpers. Keep every kernel variant k in [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6] as its own SYCL kernel, computed on the SYCL device, and keep the program's contract: `build/candidate <input> <output> B T C NH` reads the inputs and writes each variant's outputs in order as raw float32, exactly as the CUDA main does. A hidden reference checks the output (atol 0.001 + rtol FLT_EPSILON*|ref|, llm.c's own fp32 rule). Success requires compile, verify and a zero-helper scan_helpers of the whole work directory (path '.') on the same sources: migrate's output under migrated/ counts, so delete it (delete_file) once your own port is done. migrate's output can be long: read it in parts (read_file offset/limit) or work from the CUDA harness. cuBLAS calls go to oneMath (oneapi::math::blas, #include <oneapi/math.hpp>; the compile flags already link -lonemath), not to oneapi::mkl product APIs. Use oneapi::math::blas::column_major, as cuBLAS itself is column-major (swap the operands for row-major data): oneMath's cuBLAS backend does not implement row_major, so a row_major call aborts on NVIDIA GPUs even though it runs on the CPU.

museport.note: B=2, T=128 (llm.c: B=8, T=1024); C=768, NH=12 as in llm.c. Only out is compared, as llm.c does for every variant (it checks att and preatt for some variants only). Tolerance 1e-3 is llm.c's for variants 1-4; 5-6 (1e-2 in llm.c, for bf16) run in fp32 here and are held to 1e-3. Variant 6 skips its permutes only after llm.c's first validation run, so here it computes the same as 5. cuBLAS runs in fp32 (CUBLAS_DEFAULT_MATH). Variant 10 (cuDNN) is not built: it needs ENABLE_CUDNN. llm.c's file only builds in bf16; the fp32 build defines CUBLAS_LOWP as CUDA_R_32F (an option common.h's comment names) and CUBLAS_LOWP_COMPUTE as CUBLAS_COMPUTE_32F.
